Portfolio Finance – Execution Business Officer, VP

Onsite: Boston, MA

 

Who we are looking for

The Execution, Financing & Clearing Portfolio Finance team supports our Agency Lending, Prime Services, Secured Financing and Execution businesses with a focus on portfolio analytics, revenue & resource optimization and market insights. We serve at the intersection of data, reporting and scenario analysis to deliver actionable intelligence that improves decision making.

 

Why this role is important to us

The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Markets (SSM). When owners and managers of institutional assets need research, trading, securities lending and innovative portfolio strategies, they turn to the SSM business unit. As our investment research and trading arm, SSM’s number one goal is to enhance and preserve our clients’ portfolio values by applying technology, optimizing trading, and linking asset classes and markets across the world. Join us if making your mark in the capital markets industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.

 

What you will be responsible for

Serve as strategic advisor to the Execution business owners, working closely with executive leaders and supporting functions to drive strategy, growth, profitability and market expansion

Develop a deep understanding of business drivers, including revenue, expense & balance sheet attributions

Oversee quarterly and annual financial planning in collaboration with Markets CFO and Investor Relations

Empower Client Management and Trading with portfolio analytics, scenario analysis and optimization tools in collaboration with Portfolio Finance quantitative leads

Create in-depth market research and competitive analysis to identify opportunities, trends, and challenges

 

What we value

A dynamic problem solver – consistently utilizes a solution driven mindset

A trusted advisor with the tenacity and business acumen to provide thought leadership and deliver positive commercial outcomes in both the short and long-

Ambitious and driven to deliver business strategy transformation informed by expertise in market and competitor trends

Detail oriented – understands the nuances that can impact overall outcomes

A strong influencer and thoughtful communicator who can express complex ideas in simple, practical terms

Ability to learn quickly, juggle multiple projects, and work autonomously

Entrepreneurial and self-directed – operates as an owner

 

Education & Preferred Qualifications

8+ years of experience in Financial Services or Management Consulting required

Comfortability with modern data management tools (e.g., Databricks)

Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools

title: Portfolio Governance Lead, VP
description:
Technology Risk & Control

Role Summary

The Portfolio Governance Lead provides centralized governance and execution oversight across a portfolio of Market applications, ensuring technology risk, control remediation, regulatory commitments, and strategic remediation initiatives are effectively managed and reported.

The role maintains the integrated portfolio view, drives governance cadence, manages RAID and escalation processes, and provides senior leadership with clear visibility into material risk exposure, remediation progress, emerging concerns, dependencies, and decisions required.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Governance

Maintain the integrated Risk & Control portfolio across 500+ applications.

Establish consistent governance standards, reporting requirements, milestones, and escalation criteria.

Coordinate activities across Risk Remediation Project Managers, application owners, cybersecurity, infrastructure, IAM, third-party risk, audit, and control teams.

Ensure priority risks have a clear accountable owner, path to green, target date, milestones, dependencies, and closure criteria. These fields align with the portfolio operating model already established in Application_Risk_and_Vulnerability_Operating_Model.docx. [Applicatio...ting_Model | Word]

Executive Reporting

Produce concise executive dashboards and portfolio-level reporting covering:
Material risk exposure

P1/P2 and overdue remediation

Aging risks and control gaps

Milestone slippage

Forecast confidence

Regulatory and audit commitments

Vendor/platform dependencies

Decisions and executive intervention required

Translate detailed remediation activity into clear senior-management reporting focused on exposure, trajectory, accountability, and required decisions.

RAID & Dependency Management

Maintain the portfolio-level Risks, Actions, Issues and Dependencies (RAID) framework.

Identify systemic or cross-application risks that cannot be resolved within individual workstreams.

Track dependencies involving shared infrastructure, cybersecurity, IAM, vendors, funding, resources, and technology platforms.

Drive accountability for overdue actions and unresolved blockers.

Escalation Management

Establish clear escalation thresholds for material exposure, missed commitments, regulatory deadlines, inadequate remediation plans, and unresolved dependencies.

Escalate issues through the appropriate risk and technology governance forums.

Ensure escalations clearly state business/risk impact, accountable owner, corrective action, target date, blocker, and decision required.

Governance Calendar

Own and coordinate the Risk & Control governance cadence, including:

Daily: Critical/P1 exception management

Weekly: Portfolio remediation and execution review

Biweekly: High-risk and control-domain reviews

Monthly: Risk & Control Remediation Council

Quarterly: Executive portfolio and operating-model review

This cadence is consistent with the governance structure established in Application_Risk_Vulnerability_Executive_Operating_Model.pptx. [Applicatio...ting_Model | PowerPoint]

Remediation & Closure Oversight

Challenge remediation plans that lack credible milestones, ownership, dependencies, or target dates.

Monitor delivery against agreed paths to green.

Coordinate with control owners to ensure remediation evidence supports closure.

Ensure items are not reported as closed until required evidence and validation are complete.

Key Deliverables

Enterprise application Risk & Control portfolio dashboard

Executive monthly reporting

Integrated RAID and dependency register

Governance calendar

Decision and escalation log

Remediation milestone reporting

Aging and overdue-risk reporting

Regulatory/audit commitment tracking

Portfolio-level risk heatmaps

Executive briefing materials

Experience & Skills

7+ years of experience in technology risk, program/project management, cybersecurity, infrastructure, audit, controls, or technology governance.

Experience managing large technology portfolios in a regulated environment.

Strong understanding of risk remediation, IAM/PAM, vulnerability management, infrastructure risk, third-party risk, audit, and regulatory commitments.

Strong executive communication and presentation skills.

Demonstrated ability to drive accountability across teams without necessarily having direct management authority.

Strong experience with RAID management, portfolio reporting, governance forums, dependency management, and executive escalation.

PMP, PRINCE2, Agile, ITIL, risk, or related professional certification preferred.

Success Measures

Success should be measured by risk outcomes rather than number of applications administered, including:

Reduction in aged and overdue risks

Percentage of priority issues with credible paths to green

Reduction in missed remediation commitments

Timeliness of escalations

Closure evidence quality

Forecast accuracy

Reduction in risks without accountable owners

Timely resolution of cross-team dependencies

Quality and accuracy of executive reporting

$120,000 - $217,500 Annual

Director, Technical Program Management
description:
About GitHub

GitHub is the world’s leading platform for agentic software development — powered by Copilot to build, scale, and deliver secure software. Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.

Locations

In this role you can work from Remote, United States

Overview

GitHub is looking for a director to help lead GitHub’s Technical Program Management team in our Engineering organization. You should be an ambitious, passionate, technical, and collaborative leader with a strong background in empowering high performing teams and an ability to deliver results through technical programs. 


The Director, TPM will strengthen TPM's role as a trusted integrator, driving clarity, accountability, and execution across complex, cross-functional initiatives. They will help teams frame problems, align stakeholders, and accelerate decision-making while raising the effectiveness of TPMs and scaling their influence across the company. This director will foster a culture of ownership, bias for action, and operational excellence, ensuring execution remains tightly aligned with strategic priorities. 


Responsibilities

Opportunity and Solutions Identification 

  • Demonstrates and builds experiences across multiple groups or divisions. Leads and coaches teams to develop problem statements and form hypotheses for products and services across divisional boundaries to address highly complex business, program, customer needs, and/or market opportunities; identifies dependencies of other features. 

  • Determines and leads process improvements to quickly scope insights, and drives change management initiatives. Uses industry understanding to direct teams to ensure alignment between the customer, the market, internal stakeholders, senior leadership, and the goals and strategy of GitHub. 

  • Holds teams accountable for collaborating with others (e.g., Engineering, Marketing, Design) to ensure that they can satisfy customer requirements. Provides expertise to help teams validate the market size and opportunity of greatest value for the company. Facilitates collaboration between their team and other partner teams to bring about solutions. 

 

Program Planning and Success 

  • Provides expertise to help teams define the multiple program goals and prioritization for the products and services they own. Guides teams to translate the needs of the organization and other teams into program goals and prioritize deliverables based on data insights.  

  • Guides teams to engage in active risk management (proactive and reactive) to identify risks and propose mitigations for risks using data (e.g., telemetry, usage, net satisfaction, customer satisfaction). 

  • Coaches teams to define success criteria and performance metrics (e.g., Objectives and Key Results [OKRs], Key Performance Indicators [KPIs] such as quality and performance) of products, services and works with engineering to ensure needed telemetry is developed. Provides expert knowledge to help teams deeply understand the return on investment. 

  

Program/Service Development 

  • Acts as a subject matter expert in orchestrating and integrating efforts for the development and implementation process of product, services on large cross functional projects with internal teams and external partners. Drives teams to collaborate and coordinate across teams and perspectives to ensure alignment on product management and release, including tradeoffs, adjustments, and improvements as feasible. 

  • Guides teams to partner with the engineering team to contribute, prioritize, and deliver on the roadmap for product, service. Drives teams to understand the value proposition for the feature(s)/feature areas and answer technical questions on the feature(s)/feature areas they own.  

  • Guides teams to justify capacity requirements and advocate for the right resource allocation. Partners with the Engineering team to know the feature capabilities in alignment with the goal updates and associated tradeoffs. 

  • Guides teams tracking, coordinating, and communicating end-to-end project schedules for products, services. Ensures teams establish and monitor processes, and hold other stakeholders accountable for following the established schedule and processes. 

  • Guides teams when tracking and managing dependencies to enable cohesive, connected user scenarios, and to avoid issues and mitigate risks. Coaches teams to make adjustments or course corrections when projects are not aligned to schedules or goals. 

  • Drives teams to develop the staging and implementation plan for piloting/release in alignment with Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for products, services, its development timeline, and the introduction to the different programs. Ensures teams collaborate with stakeholders to monitor progress and adjust as needed. 

  • Helps teams lead governance programs and processes to ensure that specific performance requirements and standards are met throughout the development lifecycle (e.g., quality, compliance, privacy, security, safety, accessibility). 

 

Continuous Improvement 

  • Provides expertise to help teams partner with others to collect performance metrics (e.g., Key Performance Indicators [KPIs] such as usage, quality, speed, and cost), monitor and report on progress (e.g., business reviews), and derive insights that lead to productive courses of action. 

  • Ensures teams share insights with Engineering and other partners. Leads teams to form hypotheses to technical needs, perform experiments, and iterate to drive improvement in specific performance metrics that have measurable impact. 


Qualifications

Required Qualifications 

  • 8+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development

    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Math, Business, or related field AND 6+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development
    • OR Master's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Math, Business, or related field AND 4+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years experience in managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • 10+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development

    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Math, Business, or related field AND 10+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development
    • OR Master's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Math, Business, or related field AND 8+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development
    • OR Doctorate in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Math, Business, or related field AND 6+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years people management experience.
  • 4+ years experience designing, building, or supporting software systems. 

Compensation Range

The base salary range for this job is USD $140,400.00 - USD $372,300.00 /Yr.

These pay ranges are intended to cover roles based across the United States. An individual's base pay depends on various factors including geographical location and review of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant. In addition, certain roles also have the opportunity to earn sales incentives based on revenue or utilization, depending on the terms of the plan and the employee's role.

description:
About GitHub

GitHub is the world’s leading platform for agentic software development — powered by Copilot to build, scale, and deliver secure software. Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.

Locations

In this role you can work from Remote, United States

Overview

GitHub is transforming how the world builds secure software, and we are looking for a Staff Bug Bounty Manager to lead and grow GitHub's Bug Bounty program. Bug Bounty is one of the most visible parts of our security posture: it's how thousands of external researchers engage directly with GitHub to find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities across all our products.  

 

This is a hybrid role: part program manager, part security researcher. You will own the strategy, scope, SLAs, and vendor relationships that make the program run, while also rolling up your sleeves to triage incoming reports alongside the team and engage directly with the external researcher community as a credible technical peer. You'll partner closely with Incident Response and Product Security teams remediation and with Engineering teams across GitHub's product surface as vulnerabilities are found and fixed. You will be equally comfortable triaging security findings, managing a team and building a community of security researchers. 


Responsibilities

Program Ownership and Strategy 

  • Own the Bug Bounty program's strategy, scope definition, and rules of engagement (in-scope products and domains, reward tiers, safe harbor terms), keeping them current as GitHub's product surface grows. 

  • Own vendor relationships and contracts, including renewal, researcher payout operations, and escalation when platform or contractual issues block payouts. 

  • Define and drive the program's KPIs (triage SLA performance, time-to-first-response, time-to-payout, researcher satisfaction, submission-to-valid-finding ratio), using them to identify where process or staffing investment is needed. 

  • Manage payout tiers and severity calibration using CVSS and GitHub's own impact criteria, ensuring consistent, defensible payout decisions across the team. 

Hands-On Triage and Research 

  • Triage incoming bug bounty submissions alongside the team: validate severity and impact, reproduce findings, and make initial disposition calls on contested or ambiguous reports. 

  • Maintain the technical depth to engage credibly with sophisticated external researchers, including on novel attack classes relevant to GitHub's platform and to AI/Copilot-adjacent surfaces. 

  • Apply diagnostic expertise across GitHub's technologies to identify how findings interact with existing controls, and contribute to root-cause and trend analysis across submissions. 

Researcher and Community Engagement 

  • Serve as GitHub's primary point of contact for the external researcher community: build and maintain trust, communicate program changes, and represent GitHub at security research conferences and forums as appropriate. 

  • Develop feedback channels with researchers and translate that feedback into program and product security improvements. 

  • Partner with Product Security and Incident Response teams to hand off validated findings cleanly into incident response and remediation tracking, keeping the triage/remediation boundary clear as both teams scale. 

Collaboration and Communication 

  • Translate technical vulnerability findings into clear guidance for non-technical stakeholders, including Engineering leadership and Legal/CELA. 

  • Partner with Legal/CELA on payout terms, safe harbor language, and disclosure obligations tied to bug bounty submissions. 

  • Coordinate with Engineering teams across GitHub's product surface to ensure findings are routed, prioritized, and remediated. 

People and Team Building 

  • Hire, develop, and manage the Bug Bounty team as it matures and evolves. 

  • Build the operational rigor (staffing model, SLAs, on-call/triage coverage) and automation that keeps the program sustainable as submission volume continues to grow. 


Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, or relevant area  

    • OR Associate's Degree AND 6+ years experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, or relevant area 

    • OR Bachelor's Degree AND 5+ years experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, or relevant area 

    • OR Master's Degree AND 3+ years experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, or relevant area 

    • OR Doctorate AND 1+ year(s) experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, or relevant area 

    • OR equivalent experience. 

  • 3+ years experience in bug bounty operations, vulnerability disclosure programs, or security research, including direct platform experience (e.g., HackerOne, Bugcrowd). 

  • 1+ years direct experience triaging vulnerability reports for severity, validity, and impact, including use of CVSS or comparable severity frameworks. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • 2+ years people management experience, or demonstrated readiness to take on people management as the program and team grow. 

  • Credited author on 1+ published article(s)/paper(s), or speaker/presenter at a security-related conference. 

  • Experience owning a vendor/platform relationship and contract (e.g., HackerOne, Bugcrowd), including payout operations. 

  • Familiarity with GitHub's products, platform, and developer ecosystem, including GHES, GHEC, npm, and Copilot. 

  • 1+ year(s) experience working with GitHub and/or open source software. 

  • Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH), Offensive Security Certified Professional (OSCP), or other relevant certification.

location: Denver, CO - US, Colorado; Dallas, TX - US, Texas, United States
description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role

Crusoe is scaling one of the fastest-growing global workplace and data center portfolios in the industry, with active real estate initiatives spanning San Francisco, Denver, London, Tel Aviv, Bellevue, and beyond, alongside a rapidly expanding global data center footprint. We're looking for a Senior Director, Real Estate & Portfolio Strategy to lead the strategy, execution, and financial management of our global co-location, manufacturing office and data center lease portfolio.

Reporting directly to the VP, DIG Operations, this role will be a critical partner in aligning our real estate strategy with business growth, headcount planning, employee experience, and long-term financial objectives across both corporate office, co-location, manufacturing and data center real estate. You'll work closely with our exclusive global brokerage partner, Legal, Finance, People, Data Center Operations, and business leaders to deliver thoughtful, data-driven real estate solutions that support Crusoe's continued expansion.

This is an exciting opportunity for a senior real estate leader who thrives on managing multiple concurrent transactions across office, manufacturing and data center/colocation portfolios, enjoys the financial and analytical side of commercial real estate, and wants to build scalable portfolio strategies, lease governance, and audit processes for a rapidly growing global company.

 

What You'll Be Working On

 

• Portfolio Strategy and Asset Management: by partnering with Finance, People, Workplace, and Data Center Operations leadership to translate hiring forecasts, capacity plans, and space/power utilization into real estate recommendations. Evaluate expansion, consolidation, renewal, and exit opportunities across global office and data center markets.

• Lease Portfolio Management: own the master lease abstract database across all locations, tracking key dates, terms, options, renewal windows, and obligations to ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

• Lease Review & Abstracting: lead comprehensive lease review and abstracting for new and existing leases, including manufacturing office, data center, and cloud colocation agreements — abstracting key business, financial, and legal terms into standardized formats for portfolio-wide tracking and reporting.

• Transaction Execution: manage end-to-end real estate transactions — including new office and manufacturing leases, renewals, subleases, expansions, contractions, and terminations — in close partnership with our brokers and legal counsel.

• Cloud Colocation & Data Center Lease Management: lead ongoing lease management for cloud colocation and data center leases, including power/capacity commitments, service level agreements, interconnection terms, expansion rights, and hyperscaler lease administration.

• Critical Date Management: own the tracking and management of all critical lease dates across the portfolio — including notice periods, renewal and termination options, rent escalations, expansion/contraction windows, and compliance deadlines — ensuring proactive action ahead of key milestones.

• Financial Analysis & Reporting: build and maintain cash flow models, occupancy cost analyses, rent schedules, lease comparisons, escalations, and CAM reconciliations to support executive decision-making across office, manufacturing and data center portfolios.

• Executive Reporting: prepare business cases, portfolio updates, and executive presentations that translate complex lease and financial data into clear, actionable recommendations for executive leadership.

• Stakeholder Coordination: serve as the primary point of contact between Workplace, Finance, Legal, Procurement, Data Center Operations, and site leadership on all lease-related matters, including purchase order and approval workflows in Coupa.

• Broker & Transaction Management: serve as the relationship manager for Crusoe's global brokerage partner, leading lease negotiations, coordinating transaction strategy, and driving favorable business and financial outcomes across the portfolio.

• Compliance, Risk & Audit Management: track insurance requirements, certificates of occupancy, permits, and critical lease obligations across office and data center locations; manage lease and portfolio audits, proactively identifying and mitigating portfolio risks.

• Site Selection: partner with brokers and internal stakeholders on new market evaluations, including market analysis, site tours, financial comparisons, and lease execution for both office and manufacturing sites.

• Portfolio Systems & Process Improvement: lead the evaluation and implementation of a global lease administration platform while continuously improving portfolio reporting, documentation, and governance — including audit readiness — to support Crusoe's continued growth.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team

• Bachelor's degree in Real Estate, Business, Finance, or a related field.

• 15+ years of experience in corporate real estate, portfolio strategy, lease administration, or commercial real estate transaction management, including experience with data center or cloud colocation leasing.

• Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent lease transactions across multiple geographies and asset types, including office and data center/colocation.

• Strong financial acumen, including developing business cases, cash flow projections, occupancy cost analyses, lease economics, and executive recommendations.

• Hands-on experience with lease review, abstracting, and management, including tracking of critical dates, options, and obligations across a large, complex portfolio.

• Experience negotiating commercial lease terms in partnership with brokers and legal counsel, including colocation and data center-specific terms (power, SLAs, interconnection, expansion rights).

• Experience leading or supporting lease and portfolio audits, with a strong understanding of compliance and risk management practices.

• Excellent stakeholder management skills, with experience influencing cross-functional partners and executive leadership without direct authority.

• Experience implementing or administering lease management software is highly desirable.

• Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets with strong financial modeling and analytical skills.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex real estate and financial information for executive audiences.

• Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with evolving business priorities.

 

Bonus Points

• Experience in a high-growth technology, AI, data center, or manufacturing environment.

• Experience working directly with a global brokerage firm (e.g., JLL, CBRE, Cushman & Wakefield).

• Experience supporting international real estate transactions and global portfolios.

• Direct experience with hyperscaler or wholesale data center lease structures and negotiations.

Competitive compensation and equity packages

Restricted Stock Units

Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

Employer contributions to HSA account

Paid parental leave

Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

Professional development & tuition reimbursement

Mental health & wellness support

Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

Cell phone stipend

401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

Volunteer time off

Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

Daily meals allowance

Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $235,000 -$285,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.

Overview

GitHub's Pull Request Platform powers one of the most critical developer workflows in the world. Every pull request operation across GitHub.com, the API, and GitHub Enterprise Server depends on the systems this team owns. The team is responsible for pull request state, mergeability, indexing, automation, and platform reliability, serving tens of millions of developers who collaborate, review code, and ship software every day. 

 

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help lead Pull Request Platform through a period of significant technical investment. The team is strengthening production reliability in a complex, high-traffic area, contributing to GitHub's service-extraction efforts, and evolving its infrastructure to meet growing scale requirements. You'll join our Core Productivity organization and directly influence the reliability and performance of one of GitHub's most visible and heavily used features. 

 

As a staff engineer, you'll be a hands-on technical leader who shapes architecture, guides complex initiatives, and helps the team turn ambiguous problems into durable solutions. You'll work across Git operations, databases, search, APIs, and asynchronous workflows while helping define the platform's longer-term technical direction. 

 

This work blends distributed systems experience with pragmatic execution — moving between writing and reviewing code, leading architectural decisions, improving production systems, and building alignment across organizational boundaries. You'll partner closely with Pull Request Experience, Repositories Platform, Git Systems, and other teams across GitHub while mentoring engineers and helping the team grow its technical practices. 


Responsibilities

  • Lead the architecture, design, implementation, and evolution of systems that power pull requests at GitHub scale. 

  • Help define and execute the Pull Request Platform technical roadmap, aligning engineering investments with GitHub’s reliability, scalability, and service-extraction priorities. 

  • Solve complex technical challenges spanning Git operations, databases, search and indexing, APIs, and asynchronous workflows. 

  • Design, develop, test, and ship maintainable solutions that operate across multiple GitHub services. 

  • Own and advocate for the health of the team’s production systems, including participating in on-call rotations, incident response, and post-incident improvements. 

  • Set high standards for operational safety, testing, observability, deployment practices, and production rollouts. 

  • Write architecture briefs and technical proposals, conduct code experiments, and clearly communicate tradeoffs and operational risks. 

  • Partner across engineering teams to define scalable interfaces, reduce system friction, and lead initiatives such as service extraction and platform hardening. 

  • Provide technical leadership through mentorship, pairing, code and design reviews, and guidance that helps other engineers deliver extensible, maintainable systems. 

  • Improve engineering and operational excellence through automation, tooling, and standardization across testing, deployment, and operations.

Who We Are

Applied Materials is a global leader in materials engineering solutions used to produce virtually every new chip and advanced display in the world. We design, build and service cutting-edge equipment that helps our customers manufacture display and semiconductor chips – the brains of devices we use every day. As the foundation of the global electronics industry, Applied enables the exciting technologies that literally connect our world – like AI and IoT. If you want to push the boundaries of materials science and engineering to create next generation technology, join us to deliver material innovation that changes the world. 

What We Offer

We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more. 

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits. 

About the Role

The Director, Product Portfolio & Product Lifecycle Transformation leads business and IT transformation initiatives that enable product lifecycle management, program governance, and portfolio value realization across a complex global enterprise environment. This role partners closely with business stakeholders, IT teams, and cross-functional organizations to drive integrated platform execution, business process improvement, and operational excellence across the end-to-end Idea-to-Retire lifecycle. The Director translates business priorities into scalable process and technology solutions that improve governance, visibility, and portfolio performance.

- Lead transformation initiatives across product lifecycle, project and portfolio management, and related business process and IT platform capabilities

title: Director, Portfolio Management
description:
WHY JOIN US?

At AstraZeneca, we are dedicated to being a Great Place to Work, where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and unleash your entrepreneurial spirit. With an ambitious goal of delivering 20 new medicines by 2030, there is no better place to make a difference in medicine, for patients, and in society.

 

Join us on this exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare. Our inclusive culture champions diversity and collaboration, and we are always committed to lifelong learning, growth, and development. As part of our team, you'll contribute to groundbreaking advancements that will shape a healthier future for people everywhere. Be a catalyst for change at AstraZeneca, where your work will have a real impact on improving people's lives.

 

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week. Our head office is purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.

About AISI

AstraZeneca AI for Science Innovation (AISI) is driving the convergence of artificial intelligence and life sciences at enterprise scale. AISI brings together data foundations, AI and machine-learning technology, strategic partnerships, process reinvention, and business-facing AI to accelerate drug discovery, development, and delivery. Success depends on connecting and scaling existing capabilities, promoting reuse, and translating innovation into measurable scientific, patient, and enterprise value.

The Opportunity

The Director, Portfolio Management will lead the design, governance, and continuous improvement of AISI's portfolio management capability across strategic initiatives, AI and data platforms, external partnerships, projects, suppliers, managed services, and operational investments. The role ensures that strategy is translated into an executable portfolio, investments and resources are directed to the highest-value opportunities, delivery performance is transparent, and financial and operational risk, and compliance governance are embedded throughout the portfolio lifecycle.

Operating at the intersection of AISI leadership, scientific and therapeutic-area stakeholders, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, HR, and external partners, the Director will establish scalable ways of working, strengthen evidence-based decision-making, and deliver outcomes through cross-functional teams and managed-service providers. The role sits within AISI Operations and reports to the Head of AISI Operations.

Scope and Core Accountabilities

Portfolio Strategy, Planning, and Governance

Translate AISI strategy and scientific priorities into an integrated portfolio of investments, initiatives, platforms, products, partnerships, and operational services.

Establish and continuously improve demand intake, assessment, value-based prioritization, funding, resource allocation, stage-gate review, delivery assurance, and benefits-realization processes.

Maintain an integrated portfolio view, identifying opportunities to stop, sequence, accelerate, consolidate, reuse, or scale initiatives as priorities and evidence evolve.

Lead portfolio governance forums and provide clear executive reporting on investment, demand, delivery health, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, capacity, financial performance, and expected value.

Develop standardized dashboards and management information that enable timely, transparent, evidence-based decisions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Financial and Investment Management

Partner with Finance and senior leaders to manage long-term investment planning, business cases, budgets, forecasts, and Run and Change expenditure.

Oversee forecast-versus-budget analysis, variance management, accruals, cross-charges, resource recharges, purchase orders, and supplier-related financial commitments.

Ensure financial information is accurate, timely, transparent, and connected to portfolio priorities, delivery milestones, and benefits realization.

Define and track financial and non-financial value measures, including scientific impact, speed, adoption, reuse, risk reduction, productivity, and enterprise scalability.

Operating Model and Process Excellence

Design and evolve the portfolio operating model, decision rights, governance forums, escalation pathways, and RACI frameworks required to manage a complex, global portfolio.

Drive standardization, simplification, automation, and continuous improvement across portfolio, project, financial, supplier, contracting, resource, onboarding, and service-management processes.

Introduce fit-for-purpose Agile, Lean Portfolio Management, Design Thinking, incremental delivery, and hybrid governance practices where appropriate.

Ensure processes are practical, adopted, and supported by reliable data and fit-for-purpose tools, including ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and portfolio or financial-management platforms.

Partnership, Contracting, and Supplier Governance

Provide end-to-end portfolio oversight of strategic alliances, AI and data partnerships, technology providers, suppliers, and managed services.

Partner with Legal, Procurement, Finance, Privacy, Information Security, and technical leaders across the contracting lifecycle, from intake, due diligence, term-sheet development, and negotiation through execution, performance review, renewal, and exit.

Implement supplier and partner governance through scorecards, service-level agreements, periodic business reviews, delivery-quality measures, commercial-health monitoring, risk mitigation, and value-for-money assessments.

Ensure partner commitments, dependencies, milestones, financial obligations, and benefits are integrated into portfolio planning and reporting.

Resource and Capacity Management

Lead resource and capacity-management practices across projects, products, platforms, partnerships, and operational services.

Oversee workforce planning, allocation, utilization, people recharges, onboarding, and prioritization of scarce scientific, AI, engineering, and portfolio-management capabilities.

Work with functional leaders to identify capability gaps, resolve constraints, improve onboarding, and align internal and external capacity with strategic priorities.

Risk, Compliance, and Delivery Assurance

Establish portfolio-level approaches to risk, issue, dependency, assumption, and decision management, ensuring material concerns are identified early, escalated appropriately, and managed through resolution.

Provide oversight of scope, schedule, cost, quality, benefits, adoption, operational readiness, and delivery performance across the portfolio.

Ensure portfolio activities and external arrangements comply with relevant pharmaceutical and technology requirements, including data governance, GDPR and privacy, information security, intellectual property, procurement, ethical, quality, and regulatory frameworks.

Anticipate and manage delivery underperformance, supplier failure, commercial disputes, IP complexity, changing priorities, financial pressure, data and technology dependencies, and regulatory constraints.

Stakeholder Engagement and Change Enablement

Build trusted relationships with AISI and Enterprise AI leaders, therapeutic and scientific areas, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, Legal, HR, Operations, and external partners.

Facilitate alignment on priorities, investment choices, delivery expectations, trade-offs, and accountabilities across a global matrix organization.

Communicate complex portfolio, financial, commercial, and delivery matters clearly to senior leaders and diverse stakeholder groups.

Champion adoption of portfolio standards, transparent governance, and collaborative delivery while preserving the speed and experimentation required for AI innovation.

Leadership

Lead and develop high-performing portfolio management, governance, and business-operations capabilities, directly and through matrix teams and managed-service providers.

Create a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, continuous improvement, reuse, and measurable value delivery.

Set clear standards and build scalable capabilities from the ground up, enabling consistent ways of working across functions and geographies.

Contribute to AISI functional strategy and operating model evolution as the organization, technology landscape, and partnership ecosystem mature.

Qualifications and Experience

Essential

Bachelor's degree in business, technology, finance, life sciences, project management, law, data science, or a related discipline; a Master's degree or equivalent extensive professional experience is preferred.

10+ years of progressive experience across portfolio management, program or project management, business operations, financial management, alliance or partnership management, supplier governance, contracting, or a related discipline in a complex global organization.

Demonstrated experience leading portfolio management and process-transformation initiatives, including demand intake, value-based prioritization, governance, investment planning, resource allocation, delivery assurance, and benefits realization.

Strong financial acumen, including business-case development, long-term planning, investment tracking, forecasting, budget management, accruals, variance analysis, cross-charges, purchase orders, and resource recharges.

Experience managing suppliers, strategic partners, external collaborations, or managed services, including contracts, service levels, performance, commercial risk, value for money, and issue resolution.

Experience designing and implementing operating models, decision rights, governance forums, processes, RACI frameworks, dashboards, and management information.

Proven success influencing senior leaders and delivering through cross-functional teams, matrix structures, third parties, and managed-service providers.

Ability to operate with limited direction in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and make sound decisions that balance scientific and strategic value, risk, cost, capacity, compliance, and delivery feasibility.

Exceptional written, verbal, influencing, relationship management, and organizational skills.

Desirable

Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, life sciences, or another highly regulated technology environment.

Working knowledge of AI and machine-learning ecosystems, data partnerships, cloud platforms, digital products, technology platforms, and platform-based delivery models.

Understanding of pharmaceutical research and development and how AI, data, platforms, and external partnerships create scientific and competitive advantage.

Experience establishing or scaling portfolio management, alliance management, PMO, or business-operations function.

Experience with Agile, Scrum, SAFe, Lean Portfolio Management, Waterfall, Design Thinking, or hybrid delivery approaches.

Experience with ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and comparable portfolio, project, financial, procurement, or service-management tools.

Knowledge of data governance, privacy, information security, intellectual property, quality, regulatory compliance, and IT risk management.

Professional qualifications such as PMP, PRINCE2, MSP, Scrum, SAFe, or equivalent portfolio, program, commercial, or supplier-management credentials.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic thinking: Connects scientific and enterprise strategy to investment choices, delivery priorities, and measurable value.

Enterprise perspective: Optimizes across the portfolio, promotes reuse and scalability, and avoids isolated solutions.

Execution discipline: Establishes clear governance and follows through to achieve reliable delivery and benefits realization.

Commercial and financial judgment: Balances value, cost, risk, contractual obligations, compliance, and capacity.

Influence and collaboration: Builds trust and alignment across scientific, technical, operational, legal, financial, and external stakeholder groups.

Architectural and operational thinking: Designs scalable frameworks and makes them work in practice.

Change leadership: Enables adoption of new processes, tools, governance models, and ways of working.

Entrepreneurial mindset: Identifies opportunities, acts with appropriate autonomy, and creates pragmatic solutions in ambiguity.

Measures of Success

A transparent, strategically aligned portfolio with clear ownership, decision rights, investment rationale, and measurable outcomes.

Faster, higher-quality prioritization and governance decisions supported by reliable financial, delivery, risk, and value data.

Improved delivery predictability, benefits realization, adoption, reuse, and scaling of AI and data capabilities.

Strong partner and supplier performance, effective commercial stewardship, and proactive management of contractual and operational risk.

Efficient resource deployment, improved capacity visibility, and disciplined financial management across the portfolio.

Governance and processes that are consistently adopted, proportionate to risk, and enable rather than slow innovation.

SO, WHAT’S NEXT?

To be considered for this exciting opportunity, please complete the full application on our website at your earliest convenience – it is the only way that our Recruiter and Hiring Manager can know that you feel well qualified for this opportunity.  If you know someone who would be a great fit, please share this posting with them.

description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

Product Strategy Principal, Portfolio Business Cadences and Initiatives

About the role:

At CoreWeave, a leader in AI cloud platforms, we are seeking a Product Strategy Principal, Portfolio Business Cadences and Initiatives. In this pivotal role, you will join the Product Strategy team, focusing on the development, launch, and running of portfolio-level business cadences for the Product and Engineering organization, and on leading product strategy initiatives. Your work will directly impact CoreWeave’s business growth, product strategy, and roadmap, and will influence the company’s leadership team.

As the Product Strategy Principal, you will build and run the operating rhythm that keeps CoreWeave’s product portfolio aligned to a common strategy. You will design the business cadences through which Product and Engineering leaders review performance, make decisions, and set priorities, and you will lead or contribute to annual planning and goal setting. Alongside this, you will lead strategic initiatives that span product areas, developing deep insight into customer needs and the market and translating it into a compelling product strategy and roadmap. You will collaborate closely with product and engineering teams and balance cutting-edge technology, user-friendliness, and market viability, so that CoreWeave remains at the forefront of the AI cloud market.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Business Cadences: Develop, launch, and run the business cadences for the Product and Engineering organization (monthly, quarterly, and annual), including business reviews, strategy reviews, and roadmap reviews. Own the agenda, content standards, and follow-through so that each cadence produces clear decisions and accountable actions.
  • Annual Planning and Goal Setting: Lead or contribute to annual planning and goal setting for Product and Engineering, connecting company objectives to portfolio priorities, team goals, and roadmap commitments, and tracking progress against them through the year.
  • Portfolio Initiatives: Lead cross-portfolio strategic initiatives from problem definition through recommendation and execution, coordinating across product areas and bringing clear options and trade-offs to leadership.
  • Strategy Development: Develop and execute a clear, forward-thinking product strategy and roadmap for CoreWeave’s portfolio of products, aligning with both market trends and the company’s overall objectives.
  • Market Insights: Conduct in-depth market and customer research to identify emerging trends, workloads, technologies, and potential opportunities in the AI hyperscaler domain.
  • Portfolio Alignment: Work closely with product, engineering, and design teams to align the different products in CoreWeave’s portfolio.
  • Customer Focus: Serve as the voice of the customer within the organization, integrating customer feedback and requirements into product development to ensure maximum satisfaction and usability.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Liaise with marketing, sales, finance, and customer support teams to ensure successful product launches, market positioning, and ongoing lifecycle management.

What Success Looks Like

Our team partners with the owners of each business rather than owning the P&L. You succeed when you bring clarity to complex infrastructure decisions and help Product and Engineering move faster together:

  • Strategy becomes action – your recommendations turn into prioritized, resourced initiatives on the IaaS roadmap.
  • The business runs with rigor – IaaS business reviews and metrics run on a steady cadence, and leaders trust and use them to decide.
  • Leaders see clearly and early – your insights cut through complexity, give teams one set of facts, and flag trends and risks in time to adjust.

Customers stay at the center – infrastructure decisions stay grounded in customer needs and growth.

Wondering if you’re a good fit? We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams, even if you aren’t a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk.

  • Proven experience (7+ years) in product strategy, product management, or product operations, with a focus on AI, ML, cloud, and SaaS technologies.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, launching, and running business cadences (such as monthly and quarterly business reviews, strategy reviews, and roadmap reviews) for a product or engineering organization at portfolio scale.
  • Experience leading or playing a significant role in annual planning and goal setting (for example, OKRs), including translating company objectives into portfolio and team-level goals.
  • Track record of leading cross-functional, portfolio-level initiatives from definition through delivery, with measurable business outcomes.
  • Ability to synthesize complex business, product, and financial information into clear narratives and recommendations for executive audiences.
  • Strong program leadership skills, with the ability to drive alignment and accountability across senior stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Deep understanding of the AI and ML technology landscape, including current trends and potential future directions.
  • Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to drive product vision and strategy across diverse teams.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a track record of making data-informed decisions.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field, with a strong understanding of machine learning concepts.

Why CoreWeave?

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast!  We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values: 

  • Be Curious at Your Core
  • Act Like an Owner
  • Empower Employees
  • Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences
  • Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and enables the development of innovative solutions to complex problems. title: Senior Manager, Commercial Portfolio Strategy

description:
Senior Manager, Commercial Portfolio Strategy

Description -

Join HP’s high-impact, high-visibility Commercial Portfolio and Solutions Strategy team and help shape the future of HP’s commercial PC portfolio. This team sits at the center of portfolio decision-making—defining how HP competes across segments, platforms, and future roadmaps.

The Senior Manager of Commercial Portfolio Strategy leads a team responsible for portfolio planning, prioritization, and executive storytelling across NB/DT, ensuring alignment across Product Management, Planning, and leadership.

This is an opportunity for a strategic, analytically strong product leader who thrives in ambiguity, drives clarity across complex inputs, and delivers decision-grade insights that shape investment and roadmap outcomes.

In this role, you will:

Drive portfolio strategy and planning processes across HP’s commercial PC business

Build and develop a high-performing team of strategy and portfolio leaders

Serve as a key integrator across planning, PM, finance, and leadership teams

Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Strategy Execution

Lead, coach, and develop a team responsible for portfolio and solutions strategy, planning, and executive deliverables

Set clear direction, priorities, and quality expectations; ensure team outputs are analytical, structured, and decision-oriented

Establish strong operating rhythms across planning cycles, portfolio reviews, and leadership updates

Build team capability in portfolio modeling, trade-off analysis, and executive storytelling

Represent Portfolio Strategy in key leadership forums, ensuring outputs are clear, credible, and actionable

Portfolio Strategy & Roadmap Direction

Drive development of end-to-end commercial portfolio strategy across NB/DT

Lead portfolio prioritization, trade-offs, and simplification efforts across segments and platforms

Support definition of future portfolio roadmap (FY27–FY28) including platform inclusion, differentiation, and investment focus

Ensure alignment of portfolio strategy with market, competitive, and financial objectives

Portfolio Planning System & Governance

Oversee operation of HP’s portfolio planning systems (e.g., Touchstone / APP):

Ensure data accuracy, consistency, and completeness

Enable robust business case inputs and prioritization logic

Drive governance across: Portfolio inputs, Planning cycles, Cross-functional decision forums

Maintain a single source of truth for portfolio data and decisions

Cross-Functional Alignment & Integration

Act as a key integrator across: Product Management (NB/DT), Planning teams, Finance and strategy, System managers

Drive alignment on: Portfolio priorities, Platform inclusion/exclusion decisions

Key assumptions and trade-offs

Ensure portfolio strategy translates into funded roadmap commitments and execution plans

Executive Narrative & Decision Support

Lead development of portfolio strategy materials for executive reviews, including: QBW, CEO / ELT reviews, Market updates

Translate complex portfolio trade-offs into clear, concise, decision-grade narratives

Support ongoing executive cadence with high-quality, insight-driven outputs

Knowledge and Skills

Proven people leader with experience building high-performing teams in strategy or product roles

Strong background in: Product portfolio strategy / product management / planning and Financial modeling, business cases, and prioritization frameworks

Ability to: Structure complex problems and synthesize multiple inputs into clear recommendations and drive alignment across a matrixed organization

Strong executive communication skills—able to deliver concise, high-impact narratives

Understanding of commercial PC market dynamics, including: Competitive positioning, Platform strategy and Cost / performance trade-offs

High comfort with ambiguity and competing priorities

Education and Experience

10+ years of experience in product management, solutions or portfolio strategy, or related roles

Experience in commercial PC, enterprise technology, or adjacent hardware/software markets preferred

Demonstrated experience influencing roadmap and investment decisions

Prior experience leading or mentoring talent strongly preferred

MBA or equivalent experience a plus

The pay range for this role is $147,050 to $230,850 USD annually with additional opportunities for pay in the form of bonus and/or equity (applies to United States of America candidates only). Pay varies by work location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Benefits:

HP offers a comprehensive benefits package for this position, including:

Health insurance

Dental insurance

Vision insurance

Long term/short term disability insurance

Employee assistance program

Flexible spending account

Life insurance

Generous time off policies, including;

4-12 weeks fully paid parental leave based on tenure

11 paid holidays

Additional flexible paid vacation and sick leave (US benefits overview)

The compensation and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, with or without notice, subject to applicable law.

Description

Enterprise Engineering builds and operates the internal tools, platforms, and AI-powered services that enable over 1.5 million Amazonians to do their best work every day — from endpoint management and collaboration to innovative productivity experiences, all at massive global scale. This means you are not only able to develop and drive high-level strategic initiatives, but can also roll up your sleeves, dig in, and get the job done. You will anticipate bottlenecks, provide escalation management, anticipate and make trade-offs, and balance the business needs versus technical constraints. An ability to take large, complex projects and break them down into manageable pieces, develop detailed functional and test specifications, schedule, and deploy new feature sets in a successful and timely manner is expected. Maturity, high product judgment, negotiation skills, ability to influence, analytical talent, and leadership are essential to success in this role.

Job ID: 10538041 | Amazon Development Center U.S., Inc.

Description

AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.



Within AAIS, Amazon WorkSpaces is our cloud-based virtual desktop service that delivers secure, managed computing to over one million daily users across the globe, enabling organizations to provision, manage, and scale desktops with the reliability and performance their workforce depends on.



We are now at an inflection point. We are transforming traditional virtual desktops into Agentic WorkSpaces a new category of intelligent persona driven workspace experiences where AI agents operate continuously alongside humans orchestrating across foundation models maintaining enterprise governance and unlocking productivity at scale. This transformation spans multiple strategic pillars from next generation architecture modernization to AI powered capacity intelligence to entirely new product constructs all converging toward a single mission: making WorkSpaces the definitive venue for human AI teamwork in the enterprise.



We are looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to own the lifecycle of the most complex cross organizational programs driving this transformation. You will manage multiple concurrent workstreams spanning capacity intelligence, architecture modernization, agentic AI integration, persona-driven workspace experiences, and new product incubation stitching together a coherent narrative for executive leadership while proactively identifying and mitigating risk across every dimension.



This is not a role for someone who waits for problems to surface. You will operate at the intersection of deep technical understanding methodical program execution and executive influence driving clarity where ambiguity exists building mechanisms that scale cross functionally and establishing trust with VPs and SVPs across AWS and AAIS leadership.

Key job responsibilities

• Multi-Workstream Program Ownership Own end to end delivery of significantly complex cross functional technical initiatives spanning multiple organizations across science engineering product business and data engineering. Drive simultaneous workstreams including agentic AI integration, workspace persona experiences, architecture modernization, capacity forecasting and optimization, and new product incubation with clear dependencies milestones and accountability. Stitch together disparate workstream narratives into a unified coherent story for leadership reviews QBRs and S Team updates.

• Proactive Risk Identification and Mitigation Develop mechanisms to surface risk early: capacity gaps service dependencies migration blockers science to production handoff delays and timeline slips before they escalate. Own escalation paths and drive resolution at the right level. You are escalated to, not escalating up. Build data driven risk models that quantify trade offs between investment timing technical debt and customer experience informing executive decision making with precision rather than intuition.

• Technical Depth and Influence Understand system architectures deeply enough to challenge engineering teams spot risks in technical proposals and drive simplification across a portfolio that spans ML inference pipelines agent orchestration frameworks desktop streaming protocols and distributed infrastructure. Evaluate capacity plans scaling signals and architecture trade offs with confidence. Influence design decisions across service teams to unblock innovation accelerate delivery and ensure that science driven capabilities translate into production impact.

About the team

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.



Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.



We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud.



Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.



We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

description:
Why Join GEICO?

At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities.

 

Every day we honor our iconic brand by offering quality coverage to millions of customers and being there when they need us most. We thrive on relentless innovation to exceed our customers' expectations while making a real impact on local communities nationwide.

 

Founded in 1936, GEICO is a member of the Berkshire Hathaway family of companies and one of the largest auto insurers in the United States. When you join our company, we want you to feel valued, supported, and proud to work here. That's why we offer the GEICO Pledge: Great Company, Great Culture, Great Rewards, and Great Careers.

Staff Tech Portfolio Manager, Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS)

About the Role

We are seeking a strategic and execution-focused Staff Tech Portfolio Manager to lead enterprise Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) programs that improve developer productivity, platform reliability, operational readiness, and business delivery. This role partners across Engineering, Architecture, Product, Security, Risk, Finance, Operations, and application teams to translate platform strategy into actionable roadmaps, measurable outcomes, and scalable execution.

Key Responsibilities

Lead cross-functional planning, prioritization, sequencing, and delivery for high-impact PaaS platform programs, ensuring alignment across platform services, consuming application teams, and enterprise priorities.

Define and manage platform roadmaps, dependencies, risks, milestones, adoption plans, governance checkpoints, and executive-level status reporting.

Partner with Engineering, Architecture, Security, Risk, Operations, and Finance to ensure platform investments support scalability, reuse, compliance, resiliency, cost efficiency, and measurable business value.

Establish and track platform KPIs, including adoption, reliability, developer experience, time-to-market, operational health, supportability, and cost efficiency.

Drive delivery excellence through agile, iterative, and outcome-oriented practices, ensuring programs are supported by clear documentation, adoption playbooks, readiness plans, and post-launch learning.

Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders by translating technical priorities, delivery tradeoffs, platform risks, and investment decisions into clear business outcomes.

Promote consistent platform consumption, standards, best practices, and change readiness across application teams and internal platform stakeholders.

Evaluate emerging platform technologies, automation capabilities, developer tools, and operational practices that improve delivery speed, reliability, and developer experience.

Qualifications

10+ years of experience leading enterprise technology, program management, or platform portfolios with ownership of complex, cross-functional initiatives.

Strong understanding of enterprise platform capabilities, including developer platforms, cloud infrastructure, shared services, APIs, container platforms, integration services, and core enterprise systems.

Demonstrated ability to partner with architecture and engineering leaders while maintaining a customer-, business-, and outcome-oriented perspective.

Proven track record delivering high-impact programs in ambiguous environments while managing dependencies, risks, stakeholders, and measurable outcomes.

Strong influence and communication skills, with the ability to align technical, business, security, compliance, and operations stakeholders.

Experience with agile, lean, and iterative delivery models applied to platform or enterprise-scale initiatives.

Ability to build and present executive-ready roadmaps, dashboards, adoption plans, and impact stories using tools such as PowerBI, Tableau, Jira, Aha!, or similar platforms.

Preferred Experience & Certifications

Experience with PaaS capabilities such as container platforms, messaging, workflow orchestration, API management, file exchange, databases, caching, identity, certificate management, monitoring, and infrastructure automation.

General Familiarity with Infrastructure and Platform services and their purpose like Kubernetes, Azure, AWS, Terraform, CI/CD platforms, observability tooling, and enterprise service management practices.

Preferred certifications include SAFe, PMP, PMI-PgMP, Certified Scrum Professional, cloud platform certifications, or relevant product/program management credentials.

 

Annual Salary
$115,000.00 - $230,000.00
The above annual salary range is a general guideline. Multiple factors are taken into consideration to arrive at the final hourly rate/ annual salary to be offered to the selected candidate. Factors include, but are not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations.

 
At this time, GEICO will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position.

The GEICO Pledge:

Great Company: Protecting customers through life’s twists and turns with innovation and integrity.

Great Careers: Personalized development programs, mentorship, and certification assistance.

Great Culture: Inclusive and collaborative culture rooted in shared success.
